content.thinking:
I'm planning the design in a single write pass: a nine-tailed kitsune fox, quadruped, about 0.8m at the shoulder with a 1.2m body and tails fanning up to 1.5m, standing on the ground plane facing forward, using absolute model-space coordinates to keep things manageable.

Now I'm working out the skeleton rig—spine chain from hips through chest to a raised neck and head, then front and hind leg bone chains with specific joint positions and lengths, checking that each leg's reach distance stays within its total segment length, and bending knees forward and hocks back for a natural digitigrade stance.

Making hips the root joint with spine chain parented to it, using two named segments for the catmull path. Then setting up the neck chain parented off the spine's tip joint, continuing the catmull curve upward.

Next I'm adding the head joint parented to the neck's final segment, then starting the jaw and skull geometry—placing the skull as a slightly flattened sphere near the top of the head and sketching out the snout shape.

For the snout I'm using a tapered sweep for the upper jaw and a smaller tapered sweep for the lower jaw, each attached to their respective bones with a jaw joint positioned to let the mouth pivot open. Now I'm thinking through the color palette for a nine-tailed kitsune look: cream-white fur with silver highlights, red-orange kumadori-style facial markings, gold accents, and blue-violet-teal spirit flame effects for the tails.

shadow-cel shading with red facial markings, shoulder stripes, and tail-tip bands, plus dark socks and blue-violet flames hovering at the tail tips. Defining color constants...

Placing eye decals on the skull sphere...

Widening the skull slightly to avoid eye-decal overlap, confirming the surface target is just the skull mesh. Now I'm shifting to the ears — planning sharp triangular extrusions for fox-like ears with inner coloring, positioned on top of the head and angled slightly outward and back.

Working out the layered thickness so the outer and inner ear faces sit correctly front-to-back, then I'll paint the ear tip white using a position-based mask on the extrusion. I'm attaching the ears to the head bone, and considering adding cheek ruff tufts using textured cards.

For the fur tufts I'm designing a simple white leaf-shaped texture that gets tinted by the card's base color, scattering these cards across the lower skull and neck with a lean/flow direction so they fall naturally downward and back. I'm also starting to sketch the body sweep path using a catmull curve through several control points along the torso.

I'll simplify and just bind to the spine chain, letting the rump ride on the first spine joint even though the skinning isn't perfectly matched to hips. Now I'm setting up the body loft with stations defining width and height along the spine bone.

Checking proportions: belly clears the ground fine with legs at 0.55 length, and with a kitsune-sized fox the shoulder height lands around 0.75 with total height including ears near 1.3 -- fox-like but scaled up.

Now I'm planning the nine tails fanning out from the rump, each with four joints forming fat plumes that peak in radius at mid-length, spread in angle across roughly a 160° fan.

Working out tail curve geometry...

Simplifying the radius taper function so the tail narrows to a point at the tip. For coloring, I'll keep the fur mostly white with a red band near the tip, treating any "flame glow" as a separate flat-colored overlay rather than an actual light effect.

For the nine tails, I'm scattering small card tufts across each tail's sweep geometry, keeping the part count manageable at roughly one texture draw per tail. I'm also planning gold ring ornaments using small torus-shaped parts placed along each tail at an angle tangent to the tail's direction, rather than a full looped sweep, to keep things lightweight.

Writing part placement logic...

For the tail tips, I'm adding glowing flame cards using a flame texture with cross-billboarding so they read well from any viewing angle.

I'll anchor flame frames to the last tail joint, building each tail's flame from a main burst plus two smaller offset flames, alternating between blue and violet textures depending on tail index. I'm also thinking about adding small floating spirit-flame orbs hovering around the fox as extra ambient detail.

I'm also thinking about adding a gold forehead crescent ornament and a shimenawa-style sacred rope collar with paper shide zigzags and a bell, built as a twisted rope sweep looping around the neck joint.

I'm not certain which azimuth faces front, so I'll locate the bell by finding the outermost point on the neck tube surface from its midpoint at a downward angle, then stick a small gold sphere there with a cord sweep. For the collar loop itself, I need to find where a plane through the neck joint point, aligned with the neck axis, intersects the tube to get the smallest cutting loop around it.

Since the loop should target the neck surface only, I'll settle on using neck2's position and axis to cut the neck tube cleanly. The neck itself will be a separate sweep from the body, built as a two-joint chain spanning roughly [0,0.7,0.3] to [0,0.98,0.52], tapering in radius from about 0.115 down to 0.085.

Now I'm placing the head sphere at [0,1.03,0.58], with the neck top tucked slightly inside the skull's radius, which should look fine. For the legs, I'm working out shoulder-to-paw joint chains, checking that the segment lengths slightly exceed the vertical distance so the elbow bends backward naturally, with the leg tube tapering from 0.07 to 0.035 radius and a small paw sphere capping the bottom.

I'm fine-tuning the paw sphere's vertical position so it doesn't sink below the ground plane, then setting up fur coloring so the lower leg area renders as a darker "sock" while the rest uses the base coat color via a nested paint function.

Writing leg paint logic...

Writing paint stripe code...

Actually, I think decals would be more controllable than a stripe function covering the whole body—I could paint red brush-swoosh swirls on the shoulder and haunch as separate SVG elements layered onto the flanks for a kitsune-style marking.

Adding nose and mouth line details...

For the lower jaw I'm using a separate sweep on the jaw bone so the mouth line separates naturally, then adding tiny white fang cones pointing down from the upper jaw. I'm also sketching curved whisker sweeps on either side of the muzzle in white, and considering a forehead decal mark for extra detail.

Now I'm adding facial decals: a flame-tear marking on the forehead and kumadori-style red cheek stripes swooshing down from the eyes, both projected onto the skull sphere. I'm sizing the skull geometry to fit the head shape and planning the base coat paint, blending white fur with a creamy muzzle tone.

For the ears, I'm layering white outer fur, red-gold inner fur, and black tips, then adding a small gold earring torus positioned on the outer edge of each ear, mirrored correctly for left and right using the local axis conventions.

I'm worried about the earring orientation being slightly off if I rely on local frame assumptions, so it might be safer to just compute the ear attachment point directly in model space using explicit vectors—defining the ear base position and building a helper function that maps outline coordinates to world points using basis vectors.

Defining basis vectors and thickness direction...

Now I'm sketching out the ear outline points, aiming for a leaf-like tapered shape symmetric around the center.

Working out the inner ear shape as a scaled-down version with a pinkish color, and thinking about adding fur tuft cards near the ear bases for extra detail.

Now I'm adding a white chin for the lower jaw, then moving to body ornaments—a gold kitsune necklace made of beads placed along a neck loop path, a red cord sweep for the collar, and a bell hanging at the front. I'm also starting on the zigzag shide paper cards.

I'll collect positions by pushing the cloned `at.at` vector inside the callback, then pass an explicit bone like the neck joint to the cards so they attach correctly instead of defaulting to the nearest joint. For the paws, I'm considering adding three small toe spheres per foot.

For the toes, I think I'll skip separate bumps since the dark socks hide detail, and instead add gold anklet rings on the front legs using torus shapes sized to match the leg radius at that point along the chain. For the hind legs I'm defining a thicker radius profile to capture the heavier thigh shape.

Now I'm working out the hind leg IK: setting hip and target positions, segment lengths, and bend directions so the chain naturally forms a digitigrade stance with the hock angled back correctly.

For the front legs I'm setting up a similar limb chain -- shoulder, elbow, and paw joints with their own lengths and single bend direction, naming each joint uniquely per side with the S suffix.

Parenting these to spine.joints[1] since the body chain has no explicit tip. I'm working out the geometry so shoulders sit at y=0.6 reaching down to a target near y=0.045, with the foot placed slightly forward in z, and defining a tapering radius array along the leg for the chest ruff detailing.

For the tail chains, I'm building each from four catmull points with joint names like tail1_1 through tail4_4, giving nine tails of four joints each, 36 total, plus the hip, spine, neck, head, jaw, and leg joints making up the rest of the skeleton.

Now I'm sweeping each tail chain into geometry with a radius function and color bands shifting from the body's white toward a red tip near the end.

Then I'm sketching a leaf-shaped tuft SVG for fur cards, layering a white outer fill with a subtle grey inner tone so the tint multiplies correctly, and planning how these tufts attach along the tail.

For scattering the tufts, I want their flow direction to follow the tail's own tangent rather than a fixed default, so they lean naturally toward the tip; I'll tint them a warm off-white and scatter them across the tail sweep surface.

I'll filter out cards too close to the tip by checking distance to the tip point, so the red tip zone stays unobscured. For the floating and tail flames, I'm sketching a layered SVG flame shape -- outer violet, mid cyan, inner white core -- to get that stylized anime fire look.

I'm checking that the glow function accepts the Mesh array returned by cards. For the floating flame orbs, I'm planning a helper that places a core glowing sphere plus flame cards at an offset frame attached to a bone, then figuring out the seven positions scattered around the fox for these hitodama lights.

I want them spaced near the front/sides so they don't intersect the tails, which trail off toward negative z, so I'm keeping most z values at -0.1 or higher. I'm also thinking about adding an ornate touch, maybe a gold crescent circlet on the forehead instead of a halo ring, sketched as a flat extruded crescent outline.

I'll add a forehead gem: a gold-set sphere holding a glowing red jewel, placing it right on the skull surface near the top-front, with a small gold sphere for the setting and a tiny embedded red glowing sphere in front of it for the gem itself.

Beyond that, I'm thinking through accent details: skipping chest tassels for now, adding gold bands on the tail and shoulder bracers, keeping the eye shape simple, and setting up cel-based paints for gold and red so these small decorative parts can use baked flat colors without blowing past the palette limit.

I'm checking texel density given total painted surface area across the tails and body, confirming it stays fine at roughly 2.6mm resolution, then moving to the skull — placing head and jaw joints with proper bone roles and starting the jaw sweep geometry with a tapered radius function.

Defining more snout geometry... adding the nose sphere and starting the draped mouth line path.

Checking the snout width at that z-position confirms the rod sits near the bottom edge, mostly embedded so it reads as a subtle seam line. Now I'm adding whiskers as curved rod sweeps from the snout outward along the flank, tapering in radius and colored off-white, three per side.

Then I'm working out the facial markings: red kumadori lines sweeping back from the outer eye corners with small accent dots, placed via decals at calculated hit angles on the skull, plus a red flame-drop forehead mark outlined in gold.

Now I'm scattering fur card clusters across the model—cheek fluff filtered by surface normal and height, neck ruff flowing back and down, and chest ruff on the body front filtered by forward-facing surfaces—adjusting counts, sizes, lean, and flow directions for each region.

I'm also working out the tail geometry: computing the base position and direction vector to find where the tip lands, and noticing the resulting height plus flame tip makes the fan too tall relative to the head, so I'm reducing the tail length and flattening its vertical angle to bring proportions back in line.

Checking the outer tails at wide angles, they splay sideways into a broad stance within an acceptable size range once flame overlays are included, and I'm verifying that adjacent tails spaced at that angle and length don't overlap at their tips given their thickness.

Recomputing the separation at 20° spacing confirms the tails stay just clear of overlap. I'm defining each tail's curve path with control points that bow outward and curl upward toward the tip, using the direction vector and angle to offset the bezier points.

Still writing tail geometry...

Alternating blue and violet tail colors should work fine. For flame cards at the tail tips, I'm placing a main card plus two smaller offset cards, sized and leaned appropriately, with frames oriented upward from the tip joint position—skipping a glow sphere for simplicity. I'm also listing out the distinct textures needed: tuft, flame blue, flame violet, shide, and swirl decals.

Designing the swirl decal SVG...

Writing forehead marking SVG...

Now I'm sketching the cheek mark decal with curved strokes and figuring out its placement on the skull by elevation and azimuth relative to the eye position.

Working out the mirroring: since the viewer sees +X on the right, I need to flip the stroke direction for marks on the opposite side so they still radiate outward-down from each eye correctly, meaning the mirror flag should trigger when the azimuth sign is negative.

So mirroring applies when s is negative, matching the earlier front-facing logic. Now I'm working out the shide paper zigzag shape as an SVG path, building the folded white paper strip with a zigzag polygon outline.

Then I'm defining the base coat colors and setting up the fur-edge cel shading for the body paint, blending white and belly tones.

Adding a golden apricot dorsal saddle with a zigzag boundary so the kitsune has a warm back blending into white sides, nesting furEdge layers for the transition.

Still defining coat colors...

Settling on golden amber for the iris to warm against the cooler flame tones, skipping extra claw detailing, and starting a rough part count beginning with body and neck.

Tallying parts: legs, paws, toe segments, rings and tail bands, cards, and flames bring the total near eighty, so I'm sketching paw geometry with small toe spheres and tiny claw cones for finishing detail.

Still working out joint bindings...

Now I'm adjusting hind paw placement so toes point forward relative to the hip position, then adding haunch and shoulder bulge spheres to give the hind thighs and front shoulders more mass and a natural silhouette.

Checking proportions against the ear height and a floating flame marker to confirm overall scale fits within the target bounds, then setting up the root hip joint and building the spine chain as a curved path through three control points leading into the neck.

Continuing the neck chain with two joints curving forward and upward, then placing the head joint at the neck's endpoint with a forward-aiming direction, before defining the skull part's position and scale and sizing the snout to extend from the skull's front edge.

Working through the eye placement geometry using spherical coordinates around the head center at azimuth angles and small elevation, calculating where the eye decal sits relative to the snout width, then starting the ear placement using similar spherical math against the skull's top curvature.

Adding the gold earring torus at the ear base and planning the hair layout with a forelock crest plus sweeping cheek locks for an anime fox style.

Checking floor clearance for the paws and claws, confirming toes, claw tips, and leg sweeps all stay above y=0.

I need to fix the TypeScript type for the radius function so it returns a proper tuple instead of a generic array, and make sure I'm only importing the THREE utilities I actually use—builder, frame, rng, catmull, limb helpers, fur edge, cel shading, ink, eyes, zigzag, and glow—dropping anything unused to avoid lint errors.

Writing imports and palette setup...

Still writing flame SVG paths...

Adding decal placements for body and haunch swirls, then starting the leg-building loop that mirrors points across left and right sides.

Setting up leg radius arrays for the sweep geometry, naming the hind limb joints uniquely, and adding a torus-shaped gold bracelet positioned along the leg chain.

I'm checking that chain points work properly as position and direction inputs, estimating tube radii at various sweep points, placing a second bracelet near the hind cannon bone, and now writing a paw helper function that generates toe spheres and claws.

Adding claw spikes...

Now I'm setting up the tail geometry with color bands transitioning to a tip color, sweeping along a chain with a radius function.

Trying different radius formulas to balance tail thickness against fiber spacing, checking values at several points along t to see where fibers overlap too much or get too thin near the base versus tip.

I'm checking tail base placement relative to the rump geometry to make sure tails emerge from the body surface rather than clipping through it, then setting up position arrays and flow direction vectors for rendering the tail fibers.

Now I'm filtering the fiber distribution so sparks only appear beyond a certain distance from the tip, tuning the fire-like card counts and sizing, and starting to build the ear geometry using local coordinate frames for each ear side.

Defining ear extrusion vectors...

Still defining ear colors and geometry...

Now I'm positioning the earring piece relative to the ear's outer side using the bone's axis, then setting up a neck surface loop for the collar and sweeping a rope shape around it rigged to the neck joint.

For decoration, I want gold beads spaced along that collar loop, but since the bead radius is close to the rope's radius they'd end up hidden inside it, so I'm bumping up the bead size and adjusting their lift to make them visible sitting on top of the rope.

Now for the shide paper streamers, I need them hanging only from the front/lower portion of the loop, not wrapping all the way around through the neck — so I'm collecting all the sample points, computing their center, and filtering to keep only the ones on the forward-facing side using a dot product against a forward direction vector.

For hanging decorations like cards and the bell, I'm attaching them via a frame anchored to the neck joint, oriented so they drape down naturally below the collar. The bell itself I'm building as a small gold sphere with a stick/slot detail, positioned just outside the rope surface using a slight embed offset so it sits snugly against the neck.

For facial accents, I'm placing a gold gem sphere on the forehead using an angular offset from the head center, with a matching red glowing decal positioned slightly lower to sit naturally between the ears.

Cheek fluff cards should filter by normal direction and depth to stay below the eyes, which seems fine. I'm checking the glow material on cards requires it not be named "paint", confirming Joint typing imports correctly, and verifying limb chain paths return proper Vector3 arrays before moving to the tail chain setup.

Now I'm verifying the tail chain parameters, catmull curve input types, body loft station typing, skull placement using sphere geometry at the head bone, and sketching out the snout shape using a sweep with a tapering radius function.

I'm checking the nose and eye decal placement, deciding to skip hair/flame extras for simplicity, and confirming no floor or stand element is needed. I'm making sure every declared variable is actually used to avoid unused-variable lint errors while setting up color constants and paint helpers.

Writing coat and leg paints...

Adding shoulder spheres and joint types...

I'll set up the orb positions with varying scales, skipping randomization since it's unnecessary, then return the finished root node.
